case_name: A. K. Singh and Others v Uttarakhand Jan Morcha and Others
facts: There was a stir in support of the demand for a separate State of Uttarakhand comprising of certain hilly regions of the State of U.P. and some other areas.

The agitationists fixed up the Gandhi Jayanti day in 1994 for staging a public rally at New Delhi for the twin objective of protesting against the notification and to press the demand for the separate State.

The confrontation which ensued had resulted in lot of blood-shed including loss of many lives, infliction of injuries on persons belonging to both sides, outraging the modesty of women ranging to ravishments.

An association styling itself as Uttarakhand Sangharsh Samity (for short the Samity) moved a writ petition in the High Court of Allahabad (before the Allahabad Bench) on 6-10-1994, for different directions to be issued to the authorities to meet the consequence of the said confrontation.

The CBI took up investigation pursuant to the said directions and laid charge-sheet against certain officers on 19-1-1995 for offences under Sections 109 and 120-B read with Sections 341 and 342 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues: Whether sanction of the State Government is required under Section 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short the Code) for prosecuting the officials as for any of the offences committed by them while resisting the rallysts.
Whether the direction for payment of compensation is clearly unsustainable and is liable to be vacated.
petitioner_arguments: No sanction of the Government is required under Section 197 of the Code for prosecuting the officials as for any of the offences committed by them while resisting the rallysts.
The direction for payment of compensation is clearly unsustainable and is liable to be vacated.
court_reasoning: We propose to skip major portion of the judgments as all the learned counsel who appeared for the parties in this Court were unanimous in expressing that a large chunk of the judgments contains unnecessary deliberations without any nexus with the points in controversy.

The High Court did more than that. Without trial, and even without considering the evidence which may be adduced in the cases, learned Judges ordered the Government to pay Rs.10 lakhs each to the dependants of all the persons who died in police firing.
We are satisfied that there is ample substance in the contentions raised by the learned counsel in this regard.
holding: The direction for payment of compensation is clearly unsustainable and is liable to be vacated.
No further amount need be paid as compensation pursuant to the judgment of the High Court but if any sum has been disbursed to claimants the State will not recover the same from them.
cases_cited: A. K. Singh and Others v Uttarakhand Jan Morcha
